page.title: Released Backdrops
page.purpose: The consumer-facing library: what has been released, where it is used, and the identifier another scenario references it by.

priorities.statement: The stable identifier is the primary affordance.
priorities.notes: This surface exists so a consuming scenario can reference a backdrop. The identifier should be visible and copyable without opening a detail view.

priorities.statement: Disclosure state is shown and is visibly derived.
priorities.notes: The AI-generated flag displays alongside the strategy that produced it, so a reader can see it was derived rather than asserted. It is not editable here.

priorities.statement: Deleting a release is treated as breaking a live surface.
priorities.notes: Consumers hold stable identifiers. Removal requires confirmation naming the consumers known to reference it.

states.description: Nothing released yet. Explains what release means and routes to the catalog.
Released backdrops with identifier, placement, measured contrast, disclosure state, and originating style version.
One backdrop with its variants, per-variant verdicts, alt text, full provenance, and the reserved regions a consumer will receive.
A model-backed release showing its disclosure state, the strategy it derives from, and its asset-studio provenance reference.
A derived variant failed its own contrast verdict and is marked unreleasable while its siblings remain available.
A backdrop in use by one or more consumers, listing them, with removal gated behind explicit confirmation.
